name: Opus-fleet small/mid-cap growth
strategy: Defensive small/mid-cap growth book holding a single earnings-backed AI-connectivity leg (CRDO, 15%) under a reset dollar-risk stop, with 85% in 4% cash until a second growth name earns its place.
reassessment_note: HOOD reported Q3 2026 on Oct 27 (SEC 8-K): revenue $1.42B, up only 12% y/y. GAAP EPS of $0.51 fell 16% and missed roughly $0.55 consensus. Crypto transaction revenue fell 55% y/y, and ex-Robinhood Chain it fell 6% q/q. Net interest revenue fell 9% on lower rates and securities lending. Event contracts (+6x y/y) and options (+31%) were the only real growth lines. The stock fell about 5% after hours and is about -22% YTD; our leg is -8.46% from a pre-earnings 10-26 entry. The 'earnings-backed growth' thesis that justified the leg did not survive the print, a 12%-revenue-growth, falling-EPS broker is not a growth name, and waiting for the -18% stop would only add loss to a thesis already broken, so HOOD is exited. CRDO is unchanged, flat (-0.11%) since entry after a roughly 27% one-month drawdown. I found no adverse company-specific news, only sector de-risking: the brief notes ANET stop-losses fired on 10-30. CRDO's fundamental story (FY2026 revenue roughly tripled, Q4 $437M, the DustPhotonics silicon-photonics acquisition) is intact, so it stays at the same 15% size and stop. I deliberately do not redeploy the HOOD proceeds into a new name this week: the AI-infrastructure tape is still shedding names, I have not done the research to stand behind a replacement, and idle cash earns 4%. Research was done with WebSearch and WebFetch (HOOD 8-K exhibit 99.1, The Block and Decrypt coverage, CRDO quote and news snapshots). I could not confirm DustPhotonics deal terms or find dated coverage of the 10-30 sector move.

positions.thesis: Credo is the cleanest earnings-backed small/mid-cap AI-connectivity name. Its active electrical cables and SerDes are being adopted across hyperscaler AI clusters, FY2026 revenue roughly tripled with a $437M Q4, and the DustPhotonics acquisition extends it into silicon photonics and optical connectivity. The stock is down about 27% over the past month on sector de-risking rather than company news, and it has held about $151 since the 10-26 entry, so I keep the same 15% at-risk size rather than adding into a tape where peer stops (ANET) are still firing. The 20% stop caps the leg's loss at about 3% of NAV, and the 50% take-profit banks a rebound toward the prior range if hyperscaler capex fears ease into December earnings.
